title: cuda-graph: add capture/replay with shape guards and adaptive warmup to improve inference throughput
author: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Add optional CUDA Graph capture/replay support to the serving runtime to reduce per-token kernel-launch overhead on long-running generation workloads. This PR introduces a lightweight CUDAGraphManager that captures a stable kernel sequence for a given shape family and replays it for subsequent requests. Motivation: kernel launch overhead and small-kernel fragmentation were a measurable contributor to per-token latency and cost at high QPS; CUDA graphs can eliminate that overhead when the execution path is stable. Key changes: (1) capture/replay core in redwood/runtime/gpu with thread-safe graph cache keyed by shape-family signatures, (2) shape guards that validate runtime tensor shapes and fall back to non-captured execution when shapes are incompatible, (3) an adaptive warmup path that executes a small number of sample runs to instantiate memory/backing allocations and prime KV cache before capture, (4) scheduler integration: batcher now groups requests by capture-compatible shape families and exposes capture hints to the GPU worker, (5) telemetry and perf counters to track capture hit/miss/warmup events and to surface regressions. Regressions observed and mitigations: initial internal rollouts showed a regression for small, ultra-low-latency requests where the warmup increased tail latency; we implemented an adaptive policy that samples warmup only for new shapes under sustained traffic and skips warmup for small-bounded paths; we also added a runtime flag runtime.cuda_graph.enable and runtime.cuda_graph.warmup_threshold to gate behavior and allow canarying. Tests and validation: added unit tests and a python integration test harness redwood/tests/integration/cuda_graph_warmup_test.py that covers capture, replay, fallback, and stress scenarios; CI runs include a targeted GPU smoke test that exercises capture on CI runners with available NVIDIA drivers. Performance: internal benchmarks on NVIDIA A100 40GB show ~18% throughput improvement for steady-state long-sequence generation workloads (seq_len=1024, batch=8) and equivalent tail latency for short-sequence paths after adaptive warmup tuning. Implementation notes: CUDA graph capture is only used for deterministic kernel paths (no dynamic custom ops during capture), shape-family signatures are hashed using (batch, seq_len, kv_stride) and include model config flags that affect kernel selection; capture failures gracefully fall back and increment telemetry counters. Rollout plan: feature flagged and disabled by default in main; enabled for 5% canary on dedicated clusters, monitor capture_hit_rate, replay_error_rate, and p99 latency. Related: ENG-2021 implements scheduler batching by shape family; ENG-2150 tracks regressions and rollout automation. Checklist: - [x] core capture/replay implementation - [x] shape guard + fallback - [x] adaptive warmup and heuristics - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] telemetry + perf dashboards - [x] doc for operators redwood/docs/perf/cuda-graph.md - [x] feature flag and rollout plan - [x] benchmarks attached in PR comments CI notes: initial CI smoke failed on a flaky driver allocation test, fixed by adding a retry in test harness and tightening stream synchronization; final CI green. Merge notes: squashed commits and merged after approvals. Risk: medium-high for GPU serving paths; mitigation via flagging, canary, and fast rollback.

review_comments: Marco Liu: Please add more telemetry around capture failures and include reason codes so we can triage replay errors. Also add a unit test for the shape guard edge case where seq_len changes inside a batch.
Aisha Patel (author): Added capture failure reason codes and a dedicated test for mixed-sequence batches. Updated metrics_config.yaml with failure_reason label.
Priya Desai: The warmup path looks promising but can we make it opt-in by default? Recommend feature flagging and making the default off for hosted tiers.
Aisha Patel: Implemented runtime.cuda_graph.enable flag and runtime.cuda_graph.warmup_threshold. Defaulted to false in runtime_flags.toml and documented rollout plan.
Jonah Kim: CI smoke initially failed on allocation retry flakiness; the added retry fixed it locally. Approving once CI is green.
Marco Liu: Approved after verifying benchmark numbers and reviewing the safety fallbacks.
notes: Benchmark summary attached in comments: a100-40GB steady-state +18% throughput seq_len=1024 batch=8; negligible regressions for seq_len<=64 after adaptive warmup tuning
Feature flag runtime.cuda_graph.enable default false. Recommend canary on Dedicated clusters and manual enable for Private deployments.
Operators: see redwood/docs/perf/cuda-graph.md for guidance on tuning warmup_threshold and memory pressure signals.
